Title: Search for 74-year-old doctor who went missing while windsurfing resumes
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A multi-agency search and rescue operation resumed today for a 74-year-old doctor who went missing while windsurfing off Tanjung Bungah yesterday, with seven boats and a helicopter deployed.
The victim
was reported missing
near the Penang Chinese Swimming Club along Jalan Tanjung Tokong around 7.42pm yesterday.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the second day of the search operation, coordinated by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) would cover 94.76 square nautical miles.
"The search area has been divided into five sea sectors and one air sector around the victim's last known location," he said in a statement.
John said the operation involved two boats from the department, two from the Volunteer Fire Brigade, and one each from the MMEA, police and Civil Defence Force, alongside an MMEA helicopter.
"Our operations team is also conducting water surface searches within a 1.36 square nautical mile radius," he said
He added that 11 firefighters from the Bagan Jermal and Butterworth fire stations, including Water Rescue Unit (PPDA) personnel, were deployed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selgate opens first private hospital in Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Selgate Corp has expanded its presence in Selangor's private healthcare sector with the opening of its first private hospital in Sepang.
In a statement, the company said Selgate Specialist Hospital (SSH) Sepang has commenced operations on Nov 11 and is expected to have a capacity of 112 beds when fully operational.
The hospital is currently operating 43 beds as part of a phased rollout, with plans to expand its specialist team over the next six months.
The hospital is positioned to serve the growing healthcare needs of communities along the Sepang-Nilai corridor, including residents in Salak Tinggi and Bandar Enstek, as well as those working around Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
It currently has 15 specialists offering services in orthopaedics, metabolic health, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, including child development, and general surgery.
Its facilities include a 24-hour emergency department, diagnostic imaging, laboratory services, operating theatres, critical care facilities and inpatient wards.
Selgate group chief executive officer Noor Hisham Mohd Ghouth said the hospital's opening was part of the company's broader strategy to strengthen healthcare delivery and build an integrated healthcare ecosystem in Selangor.
"Our ambition goes beyond expanding our hospital network; it is about building a sustainable healthcare ecosystem that brings quality care closer to communities and creates meaningful value for the people we serve," he said.
He said Selgate would continue to develop its hospital network and integrate services across its healthcare businesses.
SSH Sepang complements the company's existing healthcare services under Selcare and SSH Rawang, with the planned development of SSH Setia Alam set to further expand its presence across the state.
The hospital is led by Selgate Specialist Hospital (Central Region) chief executive officer Miranda Harumal, with Mohd Shahril Jaapar as person-in-charge, licensee and medical director.

Title: Deepfakes, cyberattacks among five AI threats identified in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deepfakes, cyberattacks and data privacy breaches are among five major threats posed by artificial intelligence (AI) identified in Malaysia, raising concerns over the misuse of the rapidly evolving technology.
The other threats are algorithmic bias and the misuse of generative AI, according to findings from a series of AI safety and security roundtable discussions involving local and international experts.
Organised by AI Malaysia as part of the development of the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030, the discussions highlighted the growing need for safeguards to ensure AI systems remain under human control.
The National Artificial Intelligence Office (NAIO) said concerns over humans gradually losing control of AI should be examined from the perspectives of safety, governance, accountability and oversight.
It said these concerns had become increasingly relevant as AI systems grew more sophisticated and complex.
NAIO said the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 recognised that regulatory oversight alone would not be sufficient to address emerging risks.
As such, the plan proposed developing dedicated capabilities to assess, monitor and respond to AI-related threats, including through a proposed AI Trust Function.
"This approach is aligned with the human-centred AI principles underpinning AI Nation 2030.
"The action plan stipulates that AI adoption must strengthen human well-being, respect societal values and integrity, and be implemented through responsible governance," it said.
NAIO said Malaysia's priority was not based on the assumption that AI would eventually take complete control over humans.
"Rather, the focus is on ensuring that humans and institutions retain clear control, oversight and accountability over how AI is developed and used," it said.
On whether the government would introduce restrictions on certain AI applications, NAIO said Malaysia had yet to enact legislation specifically regulating the technology.
It said there was also no definitive list of prohibited AI applications, as the proposed AI Governance Bill was still being developed.
However, the existing AI Governance and Ethics Guidelines (AIGE) outlined principles covering safety, privacy, security, transparency, accountability and human well-being.
NAIO said the proposed legislation would not replace existing laws governing criminal activities involving AI.
"Any use of AI involving activities that are already unlawful will remain subject to the relevant laws and enforcement frameworks.
"For example, the misuse of AI to commit cybercrime or offences involving communications and content will continue to be governed by existing laws," it said.
These include legislation relating to cybercrime and communications and multimedia, depending on the nature of the offence.
On calls for a minimum age of 16 for AI use, similar to restrictions introduced for social media, NAIO said such a move should not be considered without examining the differences between the two technologies.
It said AI applications served different purposes and carried varying levels of risk, making a blanket age restriction potentially unsuitable.
"Any future age-related restrictions should consider the type of AI application, its risks and the circumstances in which it was used."
NAIO said the government's current priority under the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 was to strengthen AI literacy among primary and secondary school students.
This included educating students about AI safety, ethics and the responsible use of the technology.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai migrant smuggler held for threatening policeman with sickle
Article:
PASIR MAS: A Thai migrant smuggler was arrested after threatening a policeman with a sickle during an operation at an oil palm plantation in Kubang Gadong last night.
The 29-year-old suspect was among 13 people detained by the General Operations Force (GOF) Southeast Brigade during the operation, which was conducted around 8pm.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the operation was carried out by a task force following intelligence on the smuggling of undocumented migrants in the area.
He said the team spotted a group of suspicious people during surveillance before two men, believed to be migrant smugglers, approached the personnel armed with a parang and a sickle.
"The team pointed their firearms at the suspects in self-defence, prompting both men to flee.
"Following a chase, one of them was arrested along with a sickle," he said.
Radzi said further checks led to the arrest of 12 Myanmar, comprising eight men and four women, who failed to produce valid travel documents.
He said initial investigations found that the Thai suspect was paid RM100 for each undocumented migrant brought from Thailand across the Golok River before being handed over to a transport group in Kampung Bakong.
"Each migrant was charged up to RM5,000 to enter Malaysia illegally.
"However, payment was only required after they had successfully entered the country and secured employment," he said.
He added that investigations revealed the migrants' journey from Myanmar to Malaysia took about seven days, involving an overland route through Thailand before they crossed the Golok River.
Radzi said the involvement of a transport group in Kampung Bakong pointed to a wider smuggling network responsible for moving migrants further into the country after they crossed the border.
He said the deferred payment arrangement could also encourage migrants to engage smugglers, leaving them dependent on the syndicates to settle their debts.
All 13 suspects and the seized items were handed over to the Pasir Mas district police headquarters for further action.
The case is being investigated under Section 26A of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act, Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act, Section 6 of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act, and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act.

Title: MRT Kajang Line resumes service after technical disruption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Train services on the MRT Kajang Line resumed operations at 7.58am today following a technical disruption involving a train at Taman Suntex station.
Rapid KL said the affected train had been removed from service and sent to the depot for inspection and further action.
"Alternative train services activated to assist passengers during the disruption have also been discontinued," it said in a statement today.
Rapid KL said train frequencies were being progressively adjusted to restore services in line with the scheduled timetable.
Its technical team would continue monitoring the system to ensure stable and smooth operations.
Auxiliary police personnel and station staff would also remain at affected stations to assist passengers and ensure their safety.
Earlier, Rapid KL announced on its official WhatsApp channel that services were experiencing delays after a train developed a technical problem and became immobilised at Taman Suntex station.
The disruption inconvenienced morning commuters, with several passengers taking to social media to share their experiences.
One social media user claimed that a train had stopped at Taman Suntex before reversing direction, forcing passengers to travel towards Taman Connaught and switch platforms to continue their journey towards Kwasa.
"MRT stuck at Suntex, reversed and stopped midway. Had to go to Taman Connaught and switch to Platform 1 towards Kwasa," the user wrote.
Another commuter reported delays on the Kajang Line at 7.50am, with train doors remaining closed.
"MRT Kajang is jammed. The doors haven't opened yet. Please find another MRT route," the user posted.
Another social media user said they had opted to take a KTM train instead, expressing relief that a service was available at 8am.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KEB makes flat start, dips slightly in ACE Market debut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd made a weak debut on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Monday, with its shares falling 7.1 per cent below their initial public offering (IPO) price within five minutes of trading amid subdued investor demand.
The shares opened at 35 sen, in line with their IPO price, before slipping to an intraday low of 32 sen.
KEB was last traded at 32.5 sen, down 2.5 sen or 7.1 per cent, with more than 10 million shares changing hands within the first five minutes of trading.
At the prevailing price, KEB had a market capitalisation of about RM287 million.
The Cheras-based developer focuses on affordable to medium-priced properties, with developments spanning residential, industrial, commercial and mixed-use projects, mainly in central Malaysia.
It is currently undertaking four development projects with a combined gross development value (GDV) of RM1.36 billion, alongside two future projects valued at RM382.73 million.
The group also has a land bank of 24.29 hectares.
KEB's IPO raised RM48.49 million for the company through the issuance of new shares, while an offer for sale of existing shares generated RM30.88 million for the selling shareholders.
The company plans to allocate RM19 million of the proceeds towards land acquisitions, RM14.89 million for working capital and RM8.5 million to repay bank borrowings.
The remaining RM6.1 million is earmarked for listing expenses.
The IPO subscription results also pointed to softer demand from non-Bumiputera investors, with the shares allocated to this category of Malaysian public investors undersubscribed and subsequently reallocated to other investor categories.
Managing director KC Lim will retain a 52.2 per cent stake in KEB following the listing, while his son, executive director Vinson Lim, also disposed of part of his existing shareholding.
The father-and-son duo will continue to control more than two-thirds of the company.
KEB recorded a net profit of RM51.61 million for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025.
M&A Securities Sdn Bhd was the principal adviser, sponsor, sole underwriter and sole placement agent for the IPO, while Eco Asia Capital Advisory Sdn Bhd acted as financial adviser.

Title: Australia, UK, Canada and Italy call on Israel to unblock Gaza aid
Article:
LONDON: Australia, Britain, Canada and Italy on Sunday urged Israel to allow "rapid and unimpeded" humanitarian access to Gaza, calling the situation on the ground "dire."
"We today urge the Government of Israel to stop the delays now and allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza," the countries said in a joint statement.
The four foreign ministries highlighted recent floods that have "brought further suffering."
Heavy rain earlier this month swept away tens of thousands of tents in the territory, where virtually the entire population has been displaced at least once, according to Hamas-led authorities in Gaza.
"People in Gaza desperately need shelter and humanitarian assistance," the four countries said.
"Yet 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border and prevented from entering Gaza.
"This situation is entirely reversible – and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in."
It was the latest international warning over the humanitarian situation there, with the European Union releasing a similar statement on Saturday.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersatu seeks new strategy after Melaka election wipeout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) needs an immediate strategic "game-changer" following its defeat in the Melaka election to turn its core Malay-Muslim support into seat victories, said its information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz.
Tun Faisal said the party remained politically viable despite contesting without the advantages of federal or state government machinery.
Official Election Commission (EC) results showed that Bersatu lost all seven seats it contested in the state election. It retained its election deposits only in straight fights against Barisan Nasional (BN) in Pantai Kundor, with 6,112 votes, and Lendu, with 2,211 votes.
In multi-cornered contests in Bemban and Sungai Udang, its vote tally of more than 2,000 in each constituency fell below the one-eighth threshold required to retain its deposits.
In a post-election assessment, Tun Faisal highlighted the party's vote share in four constituencies as evidence of grassroots support, particularly after Bersatu decided to contest under its own logo.
He said Bersatu secured more than 40.8 per cent of the votes in Pantai Kundor, while polling more than 2,000 votes each in Lendu, Sungai Udang and Bemban.
"The support in Pantai Kundor, Lendu, Sungai Udang and Bemban shows that voters are beginning to recognise Bersatu contesting under its own banner," he said in a statement.
"These results reflect a segment of Malay-Muslim voters who prioritise governance, integrity and local problem-solving over political rhetoric."
On internal party cohesion following the polls, Tun Faisal said Bersatu's primary asset was its remaining members, who had stayed with the party despite it being out of power.
"Those who remain with Bersatu do so out of principle and discipline, unlike former elected representatives who breached their oaths (baiah) and abandoned the party for positions and personal gain," he said.
He added that Bersatu would focus on rebuilding grassroots support and introducing new political approaches to strengthen its position ahead of future elections.
"Certainly, after the Melaka state election, there needs to be a 'game changer' and continuous efforts to win over voters.
"Even without government positions, power, or funds, with integrity, principles, and hard work, Bersatu will be able to rebuild public support and help restore the nation's political and economic situation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US Treasury chief demands answers from Nvidia over alleged China chip sales
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia Sunday to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than ex-CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged spy for Beijing.
Speaking on "Fox News Sunday Morning Futures" three days after Huang resigned, Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge US restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China.
The United States forbids sales to China of the most cutting-edge AI chips, hoping to stay ahead of the Chinese in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.
In late 2025, President Donald Trump did authorise sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to the Chinese – but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.
"Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese," Bessent said.
"What's more important here," he said, "is to examine whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions."
He alluded to companies linked to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company that Huang's alleged lover Alice Huang once worked for.
"And who knew? Because I mean, these shell companies were obvious. They were being investigated. And did Nvidia use them as a workaround to sell chips to the Chinese?"
Of Alice Huang he said: "It doesn't matter to me whether she's a spy or not. You know, Jensen's foibles are his foibles."
Bessent said he wanted answers from Nvidia and its internal investigation of Jensen Huang's behaviour within the next 10 days.
The United States suspects Megaspeed helped Chinese firms get around US export controls by buying Nvidia chips for its data centres in Southeast Asia, then routing them to China.
The Justice Department is carrying out a criminal probe.
Nvidia late last month said it had investigated these allegations last year and refuted them.
The Financial Times has reported that four federal agencies pushed to have Megaspeed blacklisted by the Commerce Department run by Howard Lutnick, but the department did not do so.
"Many other departments were pushing for this, and Commerce had the pen," Bessent said, repeating remarks he made Friday that suggest fissures in the Trump administration on this issue.
Jensen Huang and other Nvidia officials have agreed to testify in one session before representatives of three House of Representatives committees – Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and a special committee focusing just on China – Republican Congressman John Moolenaar, the chairman of that select committee, said Sunday on CBS. He said no date has been set yet.
"And we think that's going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed, also to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy," Moolenaar said.
Nvidia is due to publish its quarterly results on Tuesday.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia opens lower as concerns over Nvidia continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index opened lower on Monday, tracking Wall Street's weaker performance last Friday, as concerns over Nvidia's leadership uncertainty continued to weigh on market sentiment.
At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shed 6.89 points to 1,575.70 from Friday's close of 1,582.59.
The benchmark index opened 6.69 points lower at 1,575.90.
Market breadth was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 244 to 102. A total of 259 counters were unchanged, while 2,180 remained untraded and 16 were suspended.
Turnover stood at 203.90 million units worth RM76.81 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the FBM KLCI eased further to below the 1,590 level as selling is still evident in both YTL Power (-8.1 per cent) and YTL Corp (-5.6 per cent) following reports that Nvidia's Jensen Huang is stepping down from the company.
Huang resigned on Nov 12 as Nvidia's president and chief executive officer after more than three decades leading the American chip company.
NVIDIA and YTL Power have a major strategic partnership to develop artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure in Malaysia, involving an investment programme worth approximately RM10 billion.
"Despite the cautious market undertone, we continue to advocate investors to bargain hunt at prevailing levels and expect the index trend within the 1,580-1,600 range today," he told Bernama.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor flags seven suspicious accounts spreading false information
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor government has lodged official complaints over seven suspicious social media accounts suspected of spreading false claims about state development projects and public facilities.
The complaints were lodged with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the police yesterday.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the complaints sought investigations into the authenticity of the accounts, the content they circulated and the possibility of coordinated activity.
The Threads accounts had published similar narratives while changing the names of companies allegedly involved in multimillion-ringgit projects.
Onn Hafiz said the posts used similar wording and appeared to have been published at the same time, while most of the accounts had no followers.
The accounts also tagged Onn Hafiz and State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor in their posts.
Among the claims were references to fictitious-sounding companies and projects worth RM222 million and RM777 million, alongside complaints about public facilities, including queue management systems and faulty street lights.
"I have always been open to feedback, criticism and complaints from Bangsa Johor. Every complaint will be checked and appropriate action will be taken.
"However, if certain parties deliberately use fake accounts to fabricate stories or spread false information to incite the people, this cannot be taken lightly," he said.
He said political differences should not be used as an excuse to spread misinformation, particularly during the election season.
"We can have differing views, criticise and disagree, but we must not allow political differences to become a reason to spread slander or mislead the people," he said.
He also urged Johoreans to verify information before believing or sharing it, warning that false narratives could undermine public confidence and the state's harmony.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit on Thursday
Article:
BEIJING: China confirmed that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, will hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen.
"On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen," the foreign ministry said in a brief statement on Monday.
It gave no further details, including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be.
It is expected to happen on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders on Wednesday and Thursday.
The Kremlin and the White House had both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.
Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals and is also set to bring up his war in Iran – but he is not expected to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine, US officials said.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Xi showed "irritation" when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.
"He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table," Steinmeier told ARD.
On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the United States and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: The 10 biggest stock market IPOs
Article:
WASHINGTON: Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, is set to start trading on Wall Street on Thursday.
The offering could raise as much as US$64.4 billion, which would make it the second-largest IPO in history.
Here is the ranking of the 10 largest IPOs on record, in terms of funds raised. The figures leave out extra shares that underwriters can buy after the sale:
SpaceX – US$75 billion. The rocket and AI company is listed on the Nasdaq in June 2026, raising almost three times the previous record.
Saudi Aramco – the Saudi oil giant – raised US$25.6 billion on the Riyadh stock exchange in December 2019.
Alibaba – at US$21.8 billion, the Chinese e-commerce giant made its debut on the New York Stock Exchange in September 2014.
SoftBank Corp – US$21.3 billion on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2018.
AgBank – US$19.2 billion. Chinese lender Agricultural Bank of China listed on the Shanghai and Hong Kong stock exchanges in July 2010.
ICBC – US$19.1 billion. Another Chinese bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, also opted for Hong Kong and Shanghai in October 2006.
NTT Mobile – US$18.1 billion. The Japanese mobile operator was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in October 1998.
Visa Inc – US$17.9 billion. The American credit card network made its New York Stock Exchange debut in March 2008.
AIA Group – US$17.8 billion. This Asian subsidiary of American insurer AIG arrived on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in October 2010.
Enel – US$16.5 billion. The Italian energy giant, whose shares trade in Milan and New York, made its stock market debut in November 1999.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Insight Analytics' Air Selangor win opens door to bigger water projects: analysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Insight Analytics Bhd's entry into Peninsular Malaysia's water market through its first contract with Air Selangor could reduce its reliance on Sarawak projects and broaden its growth opportunities, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
Its analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said the RM3.2 million framework agreement with Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd marked an important milestone for Insight Analytics, as it was the company's first contract with the water utility and its first non-revenue water (NRW)-related project outside Sarawak.
The award validates the company's ability to expand beyond its established Sarawak market and penetrate one of Malaysia's largest water utilities, potentially providing access to a wider pool of infrastructure projects.
The agreement covers the establishment of new District Metering Zones (DMZ) under Air Selangor's 2026-27 programme, specifically Package 8 in Kuala Langat, Selangor.
The framework agreement carries an estimated value of RM3.2 million, with the final contract value and project timeline to be determined upon the issuance of purchase orders by Air Selangor.
The project is part of Air Selangor's broader programme to establish 600 new DMZs to improve network monitoring, manage water pressure and detect leaks and pipe bursts earlier, ultimately reducing NRW.
"We see this initial award as an important stepping stone, with successful execution potentially strengthening Insight Analystics' credentials for larger NRW-related projects," he said in a note.
Aw expects the utility to continue awarding NRW-related works, creating further opportunities for Insight Analytics to expand its presence in Peninsular Malaysia.
Beyond DMZ establishment, Insight Analytics could also venture into broader NRW management and water digitalisation solutions, potentially making Air Selangor a long-term growth avenue outside Sarawak.
"Despite the modest contract size, we view the award as strategically significant as it establishes a foothold with Malaysia's largest water utility and could pave the way for larger NRW jobs and water digitalisation opportunities upon successful execution," Aw said.
CIMB Securities maintained its FY2026 to FY2028 earnings per share forecasts and RM1.80 target price for Insight Analytics, with an unchanged "Buy" recommendation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang opens first relief centre as floods hit Sungai Bakap
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Penang opened its first temporary relief centre for the northeast monsoon transition last night after flash floods inundated two villages in Sungai Bakap.
The Seberang Prai Selatan Welfare Department said the centre, at Dewan JPKK Sungai Kechil, was officially opened by the district officer at 10pm to accommodate 95 victims from 26 families.
The evacuees were from Kampung Sungai Kechil and Kampung Sethu, which were inundated following continuous heavy rain.
Based on data updated at 1.30am today, the evacuees comprised 23 adult men, 33 adult women, 19 boys, 13 girls, two baby boys and five baby girls.
Among them were 14 senior citizens (4 men and 10 women) and an adult man with disabilities.
The Welfare Department confirmed that all evacuees had completed their registration at the centre and that essential relief supplies had been distributed to every affected family.
Earlier, Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said 15 firemen from the Nibong Tebal station and 10 from the Sungai Bakap station had been deployed to rescue villagers trapped in both areas.
The rescue operations ended at 1.59am today as floodwaters receded.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Potential OPR hike to boost banks' NIM, Public Bank set to gain most
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A potential 25-basis-point (bps) hike in the overnight policy rate (OPR) in March 2027 could provide temporary relief to banks' net interest margin (NIM) pressure, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
Analyst Tan Ei Leen said Public Bank Bhd is expected to emerge as the biggest beneficiary, with an estimated NIM uplift of 4.0 bps in financial year 2027 (FY27).
This is followed by Hong Leong Bank Bhd at 3.2bps, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) at 2.6bps and RHB Bank Bhd at 2.3bps, based on the CIMB Securities' sensitivity analysis.
Tan said Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and AMMB Holdings Bhd are expected to realise most of their benefits in FY28, with estimated NIM improvements of 3.4bps and 3.3bps, respectively, largely due to their March financial year-ends.
She said Bank Negara Malaysia's November 2026 Monetary Policy Committee statement further supported CIMB Treasury and Markets' expectation of an OPR hike in March 2027.
"The stronger-than-expected growth and recognition of emerging core inflation pressures reinforce the case for reversing the July 2025 cut.
"However, the absence of an explicit policy-tightening cycle and still-contained underlying inflation suggest that the timing remains flexible," she said in a note.
She said expectations of higher interest rates could also sustain intense deposit competition among banks ahead of the anticipated hike, potentially prolonging near-term NIM pressure.
Tan noted that Public Bank's stronger projected NIM improvement compared with RHB, despite having a slightly lower floating-rate loan exposure, reflects its more favourable funding repricing profile.
Public Bank's floating-rate loans account for 63.5 per cent of its interest-earning assets, compared with 64.5 per cent for RHB, while both banks have a similar current account and savings account (Casa) ratio of 28 per cent.
However, the repricing of Public Bank's deposit and money market funding costs is expected to offset only 62 per cent of the gross benefit from floating-rate loan repricing between March and December 2027, compared with 79 per cent for RHB.
This gives Public Bank a stronger initial advantage, although the benefit is expected to moderate as funding costs catch up.
By FY28, Public Bank's funding-cost offset is projected to rise to 88 per cent, reducing its estimated NIM uplift to 1.9 bps, below RHB's 2.5 bps.
Tan said the potential OPR hike would be a positive near-term catalyst for banks' NIMs rather than a structural solution to the sector's funding challenges.
"While the earnings impact appears modest, with forecast earnings uplift ranging from 0.7 per cent to 2.8 per cent across FY27-28," she said.
Public Bank is expected to record the largest earnings benefit in FY27, at 2.3 per cent, while Alliance Bank and AMMB are projected to emerge as the biggest beneficiaries in FY28, with earnings improvements of 2.8 per cent and 2.3 per cent, respectively.
While Public Bank and RHB have among the strongest asset repricing profiles, Alliance Bank and AMMB are better positioned to retain the resulting gains, she said.
"Banks with greater exposure to relatively stable, low-beta deposits should be better positioned to retain the benefits of asset-repricing gains," she added.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Overweight" stance on the banking sector, with Public Bank, RHB and Hong Leong Bank as its preferred picks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Houthis push to within 60km of Aden as Yemen rushes reinforcements
Article:
ADEN: Yemen's Houthis were advancing on the interim seat of the internationally recognised government on Sunday, positioned just 60km from Aden, sources told AFP, as government forces rushed to defend the city.
Four military sources within government forces and two government sources said the Houthis had seized control of two districts in Lahj province and were moving towards Aden.
They said the Houthis were positioned at the Al-Kharaz camp in Al-Madariba, 60km from the city.
The Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen – the country's most populous region – have been battling the Saudi-backed government for territory for more than a decade.
In recent weeks they have made major gains on the ground, seizing the Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive, while launching regular attacks on Saudi Arabia.
Yemen's government on Sunday said it was redeploying its forces from areas near the Red Sea to reinforce troops "where current circumstances require", with securing Aden and nearby provinces taking priority.
Houthi military sources later confirmed that they had seized control of the Red Sea areas evacuated by government forces.
Two military sources in the Iran-backed group told AFP that Houthi forces had deployed in the evacuated areas, stretching from Dhubab to positions near Khor Amira, over a distance of more than 150km.
Military officials told AFP on Friday that government forces had begun erecting sandbag defences and digging tunnels around Aden as the Houthis pressed southwards.
Four military sources confirmed the withdrawal from Red Sea areas after the Houthis advanced along the coast of Lahj province, which lies between the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and Aden.
The Houthis have also seized the mountainous region of Al-Maqatirah, through which runs the main road connecting Aden to Taiz, which has been under Houthi siege for weeks.
Government forces said Sunday they would "continue operations aimed at breaking the siege of Taiz."
- PRISONER RELEASE -
The Houthis have taken control of strategic positions in the Al-Maqatira district and large parts of Al-Madariba and Al-Arah, the largest districts in Lahj province in southwestern Yemen, officials told AFP.
They have repeatedly attacked the city of Aden in recent weeks, including an assault on Oct 15 that targeted the presidential palace and left four people dead, according to government military sources.
The Iran-backed group previously launched an unsuccessful bid to seize Aden early in the war in 2015.
On Sunday a Houthi missile attack killed eight people near the city, sources told AFP.
Twelve others were wounded in the attack on a checkpoint in Lahj province, according to military and government sources, who requested anonymity.
Even as fighting raged, the Houthis on Sunday released 600 members of government forces held since hostilities resumed in July, according to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
The Houthis called the release a humanitarian initiative and accused their adversaries of failing to make reciprocal moves.
They said it was "the largest unilateral prisoner release and pardon operation in the history of the conflict."
Yemen's internationally recognised government has been based in Aden since it was driven from the capital Sanaa by the Houthis in 2014.
A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in the long-running conflict fell apart in July, restarting hostilities.
Since then, the Houthis have expanded their control along Yemen's western coastline, tightening their grip over the Bab al-Mandab strait, a vital gateway for global trade between Asia and Europe.
- 'GHOST SOLDIERS' -
Repeated attempts by the government to retake Yemen's western coast have failed, leaving both the country's southern shoreline and Aden increasingly vulnerable to Houthi advances.
Dozens of people were killed in fighting last week, according to sources on both sides.
"Government forces have remained largely trapped in a defensive posture, unable to open new fronts, stretch Houthi resources, or regain the initiative," said Mohammed al-Basha of the US-based risk advisory Basha Report.
"This failure reflects a lack of political will, fragmented command structures, factional rivalries, and the persistent problem of ghost soldiers, with manpower figures that exist on paper but not on the battlefield," he told AFP.
The Houthis were "dictating the pace and direction of the war", Basha said.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in the impoverished country.
On Sunday the UN's refugee agency said it was "gravely concerned" by reports of clashes around the Kharaz refugee camp in Lahj province, adding that 9,600 refugees were at risk.
The fighting was constraining the agency's ability to provide protection and humanitarian assistance, it said.--AFP

Title: Presgo gateways proves intelligent integration drives true digital transformation
Article:
For Presgo Gateways, winning the Outstanding Digital Transformation Project (Intelligent Parking) category at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 is less about the trophy and more about the real-world impact that preceded it: years of solving the operational challenges that keep cities running.
The recognition marks a major milestone for the Johor-based technology company.
Its Intelligent Parking journey began not as a pursuit of accolades, but as a practical response to local authority needs.
Over time, that scope expanded from digital parking payments to enfolding enforcement, revenue monitoring, location data, vehicle information, and reporting into a unified workflow.
Presgo's flagship deployment with MBJBSpot illustrates this scale.
The parking ecosystem now serves over 1.3 million registered users across 65,000 parking bays, processing approximately RM212 million in digital collections between 2016 and 2025.
Beyond processing transactions, the platform supports around 100 on-ground enforcement officers with AI-assisted tools, optical character recognition, and vehicle recognition technology.
Instead of introducing standalone applications, Presgo focuses on connecting existing municipal platforms.
Cities rarely lack technology - parking, CCTV, licensing, and taxation simply exist in disconnected silos. By integrating these systems, Presgo enables decision-makers to view and act upon coordinated urban data in real time.
This problem-first philosophy also guides Presgo's deployment of artificial intelligence.
Rather than adopting AI for its own sake, the company applies it to high-friction tasks, such as helping enforcement officers scan large areas efficiently or flagging unusual activity across municipal CCTV feeds; technology is designed to enhance human judgment, not replace it.
Ultimately, Presgo's PIKOM recognition highlights a broader truth about Malaysia's smart city future: true digital excellence relies less on introducing endless new software and more on intelligently connecting what already exists to solve daily urban problems.

Title: Macron: France looking to Malaysia to diversify rare earth supplies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: France aims to diversify its sources of rare earth supplies through cooperation with Malaysia.
French President Emmanuel Macron said this was to reduce the risk of supply chain disruptions that could affect the country's factory operations and investments.
He said this would be among the key focuses of his official visit to Malaysia, which also aims to strengthen economic partnerships and safeguard jobs and French industries.
In a post on social media platform X, he said rare earth elements (REE) were essential in the manufacture of magnets used in certain electric motors and electronic devices.
"For our factories, having diversified sources of supply means reducing the risk of production line shutdowns due to component shortages.
"It also allows us to invest and manufacture products in France with greater confidence in the future," he said.
At the same time, Macron stressed that stronger international cooperation was essential to enhancing economic resilience and reducing dependence on limited sources of critical raw materials.
"The more partners we have, the less dependent we become. Our agreements open doors to opportunities, while language, culture and friendship keep those doors open for the mutual benefit of our countries," he said.
He said his visit to Malaysia today and tomorrow follows his trip to Cambodia, which also focused on opening up new markets and strengthening economic cooperation.
In Cambodia, he was accompanied by business leaders to explore new market opportunities by leveraging ties through the French-speaking community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 95 rescued after flash floods hit two Seberang Prai Selatan villages
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Ninety-five residents from 26 families were rescued after flash floods inundated two villages in Seberang Prai Selatan following continuous heavy rain last night.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the first emergency call was received at 7.15pm, reporting several houses submerged in floodwaters estimated to be 5m deep in Kampung Sekolah.
He said a 15-member team from the Nibong Tebal fire and rescue station arrived at the scene and immediately conducted house-to-house checks.
"After discovering 71 victims from 23 families trapped in their flooded homes, a fire control post was set up near Masjid Sungai Kecil to coordinate the evacuation," he said in a statement today.
John said the victims in Nibong Tebal comprised 32 adults (17 men and 15 women), 14 senior citizens (four men and 10 women), 22 children (11 boys and 11 girls) and three baby girls.
They were evacuated with the assistance of the police, Civil Defence Force (APM), People's Volunteer Corps (Rela), and three boats from the Nibong Tebal, Sungai Jawi and Parit Buntar Volunteer Fire Brigades (PBS).
At 10.34pm, a second distress call was received over flash floods at Kampung Sethu in nearby Sungai Jawi, where floodwaters were estimated to be 3 feet deep.
"Ten firemen from the Sungai Bakap fire and rescue station arrived at 10.56pm and rescued 24 victims from three families trapped in their homes.
"The victims comprised eight men, six women, three boys and seven girls. The operation was assisted by the police, APM, Rela, and the Jawi and Parit Buntar PBS," he said.
All 95 victims from both villages were safely evacuated to the temporary relief centre at Dewan Serbaguna Sungai Kecil.
John added that both operations ended at 1.46am and 1.59am today respectively, after the floodwaters began to recede and both areas were declared safe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man with criminal record nabbed for driving cloned car, tests positive for syabu
Article:
JELI: A man with a criminal record containing 13 entries was detained in Kampung Bukit Lakota yesterday after being found driving a cloned Honda Integra.
District police chief Superintendent Kamarulzaman Harun said the 27-year-old was stopped by a police team on crime prevention patrol about noon.
"Checks on the vehicle showed the chasis and engine numbers were not on Road Transport Department records. The registration number of the vehicle is also believed to be fake.
"The man was detained and the vehicle handed over to the Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department," he said, adding that the man also tested positive for syabu use.

Title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle crash on Senai-Desaru Expressway
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Two people were killed and two others injured in a crash involving three vehicles at Km52.5 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway (SDE), heading towards Desaru, early today.
Penawar fire station operations commander Mohd Hazmi Zulkafli said the station received an emergency call at 1.49 am, and a fire engine arrived at the scene at 2.06am.
He said, upon arrival, firefighters found that the crash involved a Proton X70, a Proton Persona and a Toyota Unser, with five people involved.
The dead were identified as a 58-year-old man travelling in the Proton X70 and a 26-year-old woman in the Proton Persona.
"Two others travelling in the Proton X70, aged 51 and 47, sustained injuries, while the driver of the Toyota Unser escaped unharmed," he said in a statement.
Hazmi said two victims who were trapped in their vehicles were extricated using specialised hydraulic rescue equipment.
Both were pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel, and their bodies were handed over to police for further action.
The injured victims were given initial treatment and then sent to Sultan Ismail Hospital (HSI) in an ambulance for further treatment.
The operation, involving eight firemen, ended at 3.38am.

Title: #NSTviral: Netizen wants DBKL to fix recurring Petaling Street rat infestation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A lasting solution is needed to address the recurring rat infestation in Petaling Street, where the problem has persisted despite repeated complaints and pest control efforts.
In a post on Threads today, user @robinnsoon said the problem remained two months after their initial complaint was raised online.
"Two months after my first post about the rat problem. Hopefully, issues like this can be resolved by DBKL immediately, and not just by putting out rat poison only for the same problem to return a month later — report again, poison again, report again, poison again," the user posted.
The post also included a short video showing rats scurrying around the back alleys.
View on Threads

Petaling Street, a popular tourist and commercial hub in the heart of the capital, attracts thousands of local and foreign visitors daily.

Title: Langgak Golf land rush: From RM7.8mil to RM193mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: In the rarefied world of Kuala Lumpur's luxury property market, few addresses command the prestige, privacy and exclusivity of Jalan Langgak Golf. But a landmark RM193 million bungalow sale has taken the value of prime residential land to an entirely new level.
In June 2002, a bungalow along the prestigious road changed hands for RM7.8 million. Twenty-three years later, another property on the same stretch, lined with the official residences of ambassadors and high commissioners, fetched an extraordinary RM193 million, almost 25 times the earlier price.
The staggering difference underscores how scarcity, location and exclusivity have transformed the economics of Kuala Lumpur's prime residential market, particularly for exceptionally large land parcels that are increasingly difficult to replicate.
At RM193 million, the transaction also dwarfs other reported high-value residential deals, including a RM40 million mansion sale in Bukit Tunku in 2025.
The landmark deal involved a sprawling, century-old bungalow at Jalan Langgak Golf, registered on Aug 28, 2025, according to National Property Information Centre (Napic) records reviewed by Business Times.
Occupying 92,835 sq ft of land, with a built-up area of 11,764 sq ft, the property fetched RM2,078.96 per sq ft (psf) based on land area.
It was the highest-priced transaction among the 22 deals along Jalan Langgak Golf examined.
Other transactions along the same road, however, reveal considerable variations in land values.
In December 2025, another bungalow along Jalan Langgak Golf changed hands for RM23 million. The property occupies 30,382 sq ft of land, with a built-up area of 2,949 sq ft, translating into RM757.02 psf.
Another transaction, registered on May 5, 2026, involved a century-old bungalow, which was valued at RM70.5 million. Sitting on 90,385 sq ft of land, with a built-up area of 6,019 sq ft, it fetched RM779.99 psf, Napic data showed.
At RM2,078.96 psf, the RM193 million transaction in 2025 commanded almost three times the land-based rate recorded for the other two properties.
The buyers in all three transactions are understood to be prominent Malaysian tycoons who acquired the properties for personal occupation.
A market insider said the two other recent transactions also represented premium valuations, although both were significantly below the RM193 million benchmark.
The disparity raises questions about the factors driving valuations in the enclave, particularly differences in land characteristics, property condition and individual transaction circumstances.
One important consideration, he said, is the area's restrictive residential planning designation.
"These plots of land around the Jalan Langgak Golf area carry an R1 residential zoning status, which means they cannot simply be converted for alternative development purposes.
"The new owner can build upwards to a height of three or four storeys, with an additional floor below ground or basement, but cannot redevelop the site into a low-rise or high-rise commercial or residential development," the insider said.
An R1 designation generally denotes low-density residential use, although specific development parameters remain subject to local planning controls and approvals.
Such restrictions limit owners' ability to unlock value through large-scale redevelopment. Instead, they are largely confined to retaining, restoring or renovating existing properties or reconstructing homes within permitted planning parameters.
This creates a different investment proposition from conventional development land, where value is typically driven by permissible density, plot ratio and potential gross development value.
"Jalan Langgak Golf offers a different proposition. Its appeal is not necessarily about how much can be built but how much land can be owned in an established and highly exclusive part of Kuala Lumpur.
"In an area where large freehold residential parcels are increasingly difficult to come by, the attraction may lie less in what can be built on the land and more in what the property represents: privacy, prestige, historical character and the opportunity to own an exceptionally large residential estate in the heart of Kuala Lumpur," he said.
Nevertheless, the almost threefold difference in the land-based rates of the three transactions remains significant.
Whether it reflects differences in land characteristics, property condition, transaction circumstances or other considerations is unclear.
A TWO-DECADE TRANSFORMATION
The transaction history of Jalan Langgak Golf offers a glimpse into how dramatically the market has evolved.
In June 2002, a cluster house along the road was sold for RM7.8 million. Occupying 22,694 sq ft of land, it fetched RM343.71 psf.
A year later, another cluster house changed hands for RM9.2 million, or RM360.38 psf, on a 25,528 sq ft plot.
By January 2011, a property at Jalan Langgak Golf, also classified as a cluster house, had fetched RM75 million. The transaction involved 93,055 sq ft of land, translating into RM805.98 psf.
In May 2018, a residential land transaction involving the same recorded land area was valued at RM83.75 million, or RM900 psf.
Against this backdrop, the RM193 million sale in 2025 represents a striking escalation in absolute transaction values.
Although the comparison involves different properties, land areas and building classifications, it illustrates the changing economics of an established residential enclave where exceptionally large plots have become increasingly valuable.
WHEN SCARCITY BECOMES THE ULTIMATE LUXURY
Samuel Tan, founder and chief executive officer of Olive Tree Property Consultants, said the extraordinary valuations along Jalan Langgak Golf ultimately come down to one factor: scarcity.
"In a city where prime locations are increasingly built up, large residential land parcels in established neighbourhoods are difficult to replace.
"For buyers seeking substantial grounds, privacy and an address associated with exclusivity, the appeal goes beyond the physical bungalow itself," he told Business Times.
Tan said the land was increasingly becoming the most important part of the equation.
The RM193 million transaction, he added, demonstrated the premium that exceptionally large and desirable properties could command at the upper end of Kuala Lumpur's landed residential market.
He said trophy assets differed from conventional residential properties, as their value was shaped disproportionately by location, plot size, privacy and the scarcity of comparable properties.
"For Jalan Langgak Golf, the journey from a RM7.8 million transaction in 2002 to a RM193 million bungalow sale in 2025 represents more than a change in price tags.
"It reflects the emergence of a residential address where land itself has become an extraordinary store of value," he said.
In Kuala Lumpur's increasingly built-up landscape, the ultimate luxury may no longer be the grandeur of a mansion or the extravagance of its interiors.
It may simply be owning a vast residential plot in a location where comparable land is becoming ever harder to find.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johnson & Johnson looking to buy Ollin Biosciences for up to US$3.4bil
Article:
NEW YORK: Johnson & Johnson is poised to buy privately held eye disease drug developer Ollin Biosciences for up to US$3.4 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Under the terms of the deal being discussed, J&J could pay Ollin's backers US$2.2 billion upfront in cash and a further US$1.2 billion in potential milestone payments, the FT reported.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

Title: Nvidia allies plan 'war room' to push for Jensen Huang's return
Article:
NEW YORK: Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive, and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House.
"Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang's support.
The report comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours.
Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy that raised questions over exports of the company's advanced AI chips to China. The scandal has plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.--REUTERS

Title: Ringgit opens almost flat against US dollar amid hawkish Fed outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened almost flat against the US dollar on Monday as expectations of a further rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed) continued to lend support to the greenback.
At 8am, the local currency traded at 4.0840/0895 against the greenback from 4.0845/0890 at last Friday's close.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said higher US inflation expectations have reinforced the Fed's hawkish stance, with markets positioning for a rate hike in December and some pricing in a larger-than-usual move.
"The US Dollar Index (DXY) continues to hover at an elevated level of around 103 points, while the 10-year US Treasury yield has stayed above five per cent. This should continue to underpin the US dollar in the near term," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened against the euro to 4.5026/5087 from 4.5166/5216 at last Friday's close, appreciated vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3974/4047 from 5.4046/4106, but edged down against the Japanese yen to 2.5557/5593 from 2.5549/5579.
Meanwhile, the local note traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1711/1756 from 3.1729/1769 and climbed against the Thai baht to 12.0444/0677 from 12.0611/0833.
The ringgit was flat vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah at 224.3/224.7 and the Philippine peso at 6.41/6.42.
