Title: China, US discuss tariffs, farm trade ahead of Xi-Trump meeting
Article:
BEIJING: China and the United States discussed tariff cuts, agricultural trade and other issues at their first trade council meeting on Friday, China's Commerce Ministry said on Saturday, days ahead of an expected leaders' meeting in Shenzhen next week.
"The two sides held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on implementing the outcomes of previous China-US economic and trade talks, including tariffs, a reciprocal 'US$30 billion-for-US$30 billion' tariff-cut arrangement, agricultural trade and other issues of mutual concern," the ministry said.
It did not say whether any agreements were reached. Both sides will continue using the council to address trade concerns, expand cooperation and reduce outstanding issues, the ministry added.
Following a September summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in Washington, the two sides proposed a US$60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly US$17 billion worth of US farm goods that China imported in 2024, but the plan has yet to be finalised.
Chinese purchases of US farm goods other than soybeans are on track to hit a seven-year low this year, despite an agreement to buy US$17 billion annually through 2028, a Reuters analysis of customs data showed earlier this month, underscoring persistent uncertainty over the deal.
Beijing has repeatedly urged Washington to implement the US$60 billion tariff-reduction deal, calling it a prerequisite for increasing purchases of US farm goods.
The White House said Trump will meet Xi on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI safety must protect human lives and the human mind
Article:
LETTER:
A chatbot is not a doctor, a therapist, or a trusted friend. Yet its confident language can make it sound like one.
When people rely on unsafe answers, the consequences can reach far beyond a screen.
The recent case of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Seattle software engineer who died of sudden unexpected death in Epilepsy on Feb 12, 2026, after following an AI-generated tapering plan to reduce her anti-seizure medication is deeply unsettling.
This is not an argument against artificial intelligence (AI). AI can bring real benefits to medicine, education, business, and public services.
However, responsibility should not disappear into technical complexity or be dismissed as a simple computer error when an AI tool contributes to serious harm.
One useful way to understand the challenge comes from legal sociologist Lawrence M. Friedman. He describes a legal system through three connected elements: structure, substance, and culture.
First, the courts, regulators, and public agencies responsible for protecting people. Many of these institutions were designed around human professionals and businesses operating within identifiable jurisdictions.
AI systems, by contrast, may be developed in one country, hosted in another, and used by people around the world. It can be difficult to identify which authority should investigate a harmful output or require a company to fix it.
The speed of software updates also creates a practical problem: a system may change while an investigation is still under way.
Second, laws must be able to address harm involving AI. An algorithm does not have a conscience or form intentions in the way a person does.
The law should examine those choices and the risks that could reasonably have been anticipated. It should make clear when an AI product is being presented as a source of health advice and what safeguards are required.
Another dimension that deserves greater public attention is the protection of the human mind.
AI does not only process information; increasingly, it can infer preferences, emotional states, and patterns of behaviour from the data people leave behind.
Cognitive liberty concerns a person's freedom to think and make decisions without undue interference.
Mental privacy concerns protection against intrusive access to, or inference about, highly personal mental information.
Mental integrity concerns protection from harmful manipulation that undermines a person's psychological autonomy.
These ideas should not remain confined to academic debate. Consider how a persuasive chatbot might respond to a person experiencing distress, or how a system might use sensitive behavioural data to influence a vulnerable user.
Human dignity and autonomy should not become collateral damage in the race to innovate.
Third, the expectations and habits that influence how people use technology and respond to harm.
People need to understand that an AI-generated answer can be incomplete, misleading, or wrong.
At the same time, digital literacy cannot become an excuse to place the entire burden on users.
A warning to "use AI responsibly" is not enough when a system is designed and marketed by organisations with far greater technical knowledge and control.
Malaysia, together with its fellow Asean member states, has an opportunity to shape an approach to AI governance that is both practical and centred on people.
The European Union's AI Act demonstrates how a risk-based regulatory framework can establish enforceable safeguards, while developments in Chile have brought constitutional protection of brain activity and mental integrity into the global discussion on neurorights.
Asean too has begun to develop its own regional approach through the Asean Guide on AI Governance and Ethics (2024).
However, regional guidance alone is not enough.
Although it provides a common direction for responsible AI development, its voluntary nature means that meaningful protection ultimately depends on how individual countries translate its principles into national laws, institutions, and enforcement mechanisms.
The challenge, therefore, is not simply to adopt international standards, but to ensure that technological progress is accompanied by effective protection of human dignity and fundamental rights.
This challenges the entire region. Countries in Southeast Asia differ in their levels of technological development, regulatory capacity, and institutional readiness.
Yet they face increasingly similar risks: unsafe AI-generated advice, misuse of personal data, algorithmic discrimination and the potential manipulation of human behaviour.
Asean therefore needs stronger regional cooperation to promote compatible safety standards, share regulatory expertise, facilitate cross-border responses to AI-related harm, and establish common expectations of accountability for developers and organisations deploying high-risk systems.
Cooperation should not require every member to adopt identical legislation but a shared minimum level of protection while allowing each country to respond according to its legal system, social conditions, and institutional capacity.
Asean members should translate these shared principles into practical safeguards.
This means clarifying the legal responsibilities of AI developers and organisations that deploy high-risk systems; requiring meaningful safety assessments, transparency, and continuous monitoring; and ensuring that individuals have accessible channels to report harm and seek remedies.
Regulators must have sufficient expertise and authority to investigate potentially harmful systems and intervene when serious risks arise.
Equally important, AI governance should extend beyond data protection to address the protection of mental privacy, cognitive liberty, and mental integrity.
Public education must also help people understand the limits of AI, particularly in healthcare and mental-health contexts.
Ultimately, Asean should not become merely a market for AI technologies developed elsewhere; it should become an active participant in shaping the rules that govern them, ensuring that innovation serves people rather than placing them at unnecessary risk.
Above all, neurorights should be considered as part of a wider conversation about privacy, autonomy, and human dignity. Any new protections should be carefully defined and connected to enforceable duties, rather than remaining broad promises.
The aim is not to regulate every conversation with a machine. It is to ensure that powerful systems cannot expose people to serious and avoidable risks without accountability.
A safe digital future must protect the people, and the minds behind them.
DR KAMINI SHANMUGAIAH
Head of School
Malaysia University of Science and Technology
DR EDY SANTOSO
Associate Professor
Pakuan University Indonesia
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Intel sued by shareholders following 29pct stock plunge
Article:
NEW YORK: Intel has been sued by shareholders who accused the US chipmaker of defrauding them by concealing the impact of a prolonged slowdown in personal computer sales that caused its stock price to plunge nearly 29 per cent in a single day.
In a proposed class action filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, shareholders led by a Michigan pension fund said Intel was too slow to disclose information about how slowing PC sales and an inventory glut would weigh on revenue.
The shareholders said Intel's problems with PC sales and excess inventory outweighed data centre construction and other benefits related to the artificial intelligence boom.
They also said Intel had the motive and opportunity to defraud by raising capital in mid-August, halfway through its "disastrous" third quarter, when it sold US$23 billion of stock at US$95 per share.
The sale came as Intel looked to build out its chip contract manufacturing business, a key part of chief executive Lip-Bu Tan's business strategy. Shares of Intel closed Friday at US$59.66.
Intel did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Sunday.
Shares of Intel fell 28.60 per cent on Oct 30, wiping out about US$140 billion of market value, one day after the Santa Clara, California-based company projected lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue and profit and forecast a prolonged slowdown in PC sales.
Tan told analysts that he was disappointed by manufacturing supply shortages, an "unprecedented memory crunch", and resulting softness in PCs.
"We need to address these challenges with urgency," Tan added.
Like many other large technology companies, Intel has poured money into manufacturing, but supply disruptions have made it harder to benefit from growing demand for data centre chips.
Meanwhile, rising memory prices have made PCs more expensive, weighing on demand.
Friday's lawsuit, led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, seeks unspecified damages for Intel shareholders between July 23, 2026, and Oct 29, 2026. Tan and chief financial officer David Zinsner are also defendants.
Intel shares are up 62 per cent this year through Friday, though they have slid from their recent peak of US$142.35 on June 30.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar races between Manila and KL as Asean meetings and Macron visit collide
Article:
MANILA, Nov 16 — A series of summit meetings awaits Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on the third day of his visit to Manila today, before he makes a brief return to Malaysia this afternoon.
Anwar is scheduled to receive French President Emmanuel Macron, who is due in Malaysia tomorrow morning for an official visit.
However, Anwar is expected to return to Manila in the afternoon to attend the Asean-United States Special Summit and a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
Today, Anwar is scheduled to attend the 29th Asean-China Summit, where he will deliver the Asean Common Statement on behalf of the bloc, as well as Malaysia’s national statement. Malaysia is the Asean country coordinator for dialogue relations with China.
He will also attend the 6th Asean-Australia Summit, the 16th Asean-United Nations Summit and the 27th Asean-Republic of Korea Summit, where he is scheduled to deliver Malaysia’s national statement at each meeting.
The Asean-China Summit comes as both sides aim to conclude negotiations on a Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea by year-end.
Yesterday, Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said negotiations on the South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC) were in their final stage, with provisional agreement reached on about 80 per cent of the draft.
She said the negotiations would continue beyond the end-2026 target and into 2027, under Singapore’s Asean chairmanship.
Anwar is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, hosted by the Philippines under the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together”. — Bernama

Title: Flood victims in Perak surge past 1,100 as waters rise again; Selangor sees slight relief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The number of flood victims in Perak has risen significantly to 1,110 people from 392 families this morning, compared to 191 people from 58 families yesterday evening, while Selangor has recorded a slight decrease.
In PERAK, the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat reported that the Larut, Matang, and Selama district has been hit by floods again, with the relief centre (PPS) at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Simpang housing the highest number of victims, totalling 282 people.
This is followed by the PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai (DOR) Sungai Relong (93 people), Masjid Ali Rouse Kampung Ulu Sepetang (91), Dewan Changkat Larah (73), SK Batu Hampar (71), DOR Kampung Simpang Halt (59), SK Matang Gelugor (58), Dewan Serbaguna Taman Kaya (56), SK Matang (49), Masjid Al Wusta (41), Masjid Al Hidayah (25) and DOR Air Kuning, Asam Kumbang (13).
The Kerian district has also been affected by renewed flooding, with the PPS at SK Bukit Merah accommodating 33 people from three families, while in the Hilir Perak district, the PPS at Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) continues to house 186 people from 56 families.
Meanwhile, in SELANGOR, 1,371 victims from 362 families remain sheltered at six PPS in the Kuala Selangor district this morning, compared to 1,399 people from 370 families yesterday evening.
According to the InfoBencana portal of the Social Welfare Department (JKM), the PPS at SK Parit Mahang accommodates the highest number of evacuees, 399 people, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (396), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (280), DOR Bukit Kuching Tengah (116), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (114), and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (66).
In PENANG, 95 evacuees from 26 families have been relocated to the Village Community Management Council (MPKK) hall in Sungai Kechil, Nibong Tebal, after their homes were hit by floods following several hours of heavy rain last night. The affected areas include Jalan Sekolah and Kampung Sethu.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations and Firefighting, John Sagun Francis, said the evacuees consist of 23 adult men, 33 adult women, 19 boys, 13 girls, and seven babies, comprising two boys and five girls. — Bernama

Title: Three-vehicle collision on Senai-Desaru Expressway leaves two dead, two injured
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 16 — Two people were killed, and two others were injured in an accident involving three vehicles at Kilometre 52.5 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway (SDE), heading towards Desaru, early today.
Penawar Fire and Rescue Station Operations Commander, PBK I Mohd Hazmi Zulkafli, said the station received an emergency call at 1.49am, and a fire engine arrived at the scene at 2.06am.
He said upon arrival, firefighters found that the accident involved a Proton X70, a Proton Persona and a Toyota Unser, with five people involved.
The two fatalities were identified as a 58-year-old man travelling in the Proton X70 and a 26-year-old woman in the Proton Persona.
“Two others travelling in the Proton X70, aged 51 and 47, sustained injuries, while a man in the Toyota Unser escaped unharmed,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Hazmi said two victims who were trapped in their vehicles were extricated using specialised hydraulic rescue equipment. Both were pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel, and their bodies were handed over to the police for further action.
The injured victims were given initial treatment and then sent to Sultan Ismail Hospital (HSI) in a Ministry of Health (MOH) ambulance for further treatment.
The operation, involving eight personnel and one fire rescue tender (FRT), ended at 3.38am. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina visits relief centre as floods affect 23 families in Nibong Tebal
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Nov 16 — A total of 23 families have been affected by floods in several areas of Sungai Kechil here, with some residents being housed at the Sungai Kechil MPKK Hall temporary relief centre (PPS) last night.
Nibong Tebal Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the affected areas included Sungai Duri, Kampung Sethu, Kampung Besar, Kampung Sungai Buaya, Sungai Kechil and Jawi.
She said that upon receiving information about the incident, she immediately went to the relief centre to assess the situation of the affected residents.
“Through the Nibong Tebal People’s Service Centre, food has also been provided to families taking shelter at the PPS, as well as delivered to several homes of those affected,” she said in a Facebook post.
Fadhlina, who is also Education Minister, said she had contacted the relevant agencies to ensure that the evacuation process went smoothly, basic necessities were sufficient and the welfare of all affected families was taken care of.
She also advised residents in high-risk areas to remain vigilant and prioritise their safety and that of their families, including moving to safe locations if necessary. — Bernama

Title: Man narrowly escapes as landslide hits home near Bagan Serai
Article:
IPOH, Nov 16 — An elderly man escaped injury after a landslide and overflow of hill water affected his house at Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampung Bukit Merah, Simpang Empat Semanggol, near Bagan Serai in Kerian, last night.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 7.05pm, following which a team from the Bagan Serai Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene, 21 kilometres away.
He said the incident caused an extension at the rear of the house to collapse, while members of the public helped the victim to safety before rescuers arrived.
“The operation commander conducted an initial assessment and directed personnel wearing full personal protective equipment (PPE) to monitor the area to ensure no other victims were involved.
“The victim was also advised by the operation commander and police to relocate as it was still raining and there were concerns of further ground movement,” he said in a statement last night.
Sabarodzi said the operation was brought under control at 7.43pm and fully concluded at 8.20pm. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan needs new political realignment to win Putrajaya, says Amirudin
Article:
KLANG, Nov 16 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) must focus its efforts on formulating a new political realignment as a strategy to form the government in the next general election, said PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said preliminary analysis had identified encouraging signs and a positive wave, including increased Malay support for PH in the Melaka state election, but its current performance was still insufficient to form a government without broader consensus.
“Yes, I have seen the preliminary analysis. There has been some fairly positive growth for PH, particularly an increase in Malay votes. However, it is not enough because this is not merely about coalitions or support for a coalition, but about how political realignment should be considered to form a government.
“The increase represents a positive wave, and we (PH) are confident that there is still time to intensify and expand these efforts in the future for our collective success,” he said after officiating the 2026 National-Level Digital Education Carnival for Parent, Community and Private Sector Involvement at Klang Parade Mall here yesterday.
Elaborating, Amirudin, who is also PKR vice-president, said the country’s current political realities showed that the success of forming a government no longer depended solely on cooperation between political parties, but instead required consensus among political coalitions.
He said support for the coalition remained intact, with increases recorded in several areas, including the votes secured by Melaka PH chairman Datuk Seri Adly Zahari in the Bukit Katil state constituency, which rose from 6,805 in 2021 to 8,698 in 2026 despite his defeat.
He said the achievement was in line with the trend of growing Malay voter support previously recorded in elections in Negeri Sembilan.
“Regarding the recent voter turnout, I observed that it was higher than in the previous state election, but slightly lower than in the last general election.
“There are actually many more aspects that we need to examine. Therefore, the entire party machinery must continue to strengthen its grassroots operations and reassess its communication strategies to ensure that the current momentum of support can be translated into success in the future,” he said.
The official results of the 16th Melaka state election saw Barisan Nasional (BN) form the state government after winning 21 of the 28 state seats contested, while PH secured four seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) three. — Bernama

Title: Penang doctor disappears while windsurfing, search intensifies off Tanjung Bungah
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — An elderly man has been reported missing while windsurfing in the waters off Tanjung Bungah, near a swimming club on Jalan Tanjung Tokong here last night.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Fire and Rescue Operations Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the victim has been identified as Dr Khaw Chun Sein, aged 74.
He said the department received an emergency call from a member of the public about the incident at 7.42pm.
A five-member team from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue Station was then dispatched to the location.
“The team is carrying out a search and rescue operation using surface searching at the scene. A Fire Control Post has also been set up to coordinate the operation. So far, the victim has not been found,” he said in a statement last night.
John said the operation is still ongoing, with assistance from the Malaysian Civil Defence Force and the Royal Malaysia Police.
He added that updates will be provided from time to time. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia won’t let US ties limit China engagement, says Anwar in Manila
Article:
MANILA, Nov 16 — Malaysia’s relationship with the United States will not prevent it from engaging independently with other countries, including China, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said foreign investments must operate within Malaysia’s national policy framework and respect its interests, as the country navigates an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment.
“You are an investor; you can decide what to do, but it must be through our framework, our national policy. And the protection of our interests as a nation,” he said at a dinner held in conjunction with his working visit for the 49th Asean Summit here last night.
Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.
Anwar said he had conveyed Malaysia’s independent position during a telephone conversation with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about a week and a half ago, during which issues involving data centres, chips and artificial intelligence were raised.
He said the assurances he gave during that conversation did not preclude Malaysia’s right to make its own decisions on engagement with other countries, including China.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the Asean Summit provided an important opportunity to chart the region’s course through a turbulent period marked by geopolitical uncertainties.
Engagement with different powers reflected both Malaysia’s foreign policy approach and Asean centrality, with smaller countries needing to navigate difficult circumstances carefully.
On the economy, the Prime Minister said attracting investments and securing projects must go hand in hand with clean government and efforts to prevent abuse of power.
“Good governance is central to me,” he said, reaffirming his determination to continue policies to combat corruption.
Anwar said Malaysia should be recognised not only for its vibrant economy but also for its firm position against abuse of power and endemic corruption, which ultimately caused hardship for ordinary people. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest drug-positive man after knife scare at Kedah state government complex
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 16 — Police arrested a man suspected of being under the influence of drugs when he attempted to trespass onto the grounds of Wisma Darul Aman here today, carrying a knife.
Kota Setar district police chief ACP Syed Basri Syed Ali said police received information about the incident, which occurred at 8.10am, from a security assistant at the State Secretary’s Office.
“The 45-year-old suspect rode a motorcycle through the entrance to Wisma Darul Aman without stopping at the security post. A security guard gave chase and apprehended him to ask about his purpose for entering the area.
“The suspect took out a 15-centimetre knife from his trouser pocket and brandished it at the security guard before attempting to flee. He was successfully apprehended before police arrived at the scene to take further action,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the suspect was taken to the Alor Setar police station, where a body search found no contraband or drugs in his possession.
“Checks revealed that the suspect had no previous criminal record. However, he appeared to be under the influence of drugs when arrested, and a urine test returned positive for methamphetamine and amphetamine.
“The case is being investigated under Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Mystery over Batu Muda’s poor air quality deepens, DOE deploys drones and sensors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Department of Environment (DOE) is conducting drone surveillance and deploying additional air quality monitoring equipment to investigate the significant difference in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings between the Batu Muda and Cheras stations here.
In a statement yesterday, the DOE said the measures were taken following API readings at the Batu Muda Air Quality Monitoring Station remaining at unhealthy levels of over 150 for the past two days, compared with the nearby Cheras station, which recorded readings of only around 60.
It said additional equipment had been installed near the Batu Muda station to obtain supporting data for technical analysis, with preliminary findings to be announced after 24 hours of monitoring and completion of the technical review.
“At the same time, drone-based air monitoring is also being conducted to help identify possible sources of air pollutant emissions, including open burning activities in the surrounding areas,” the statement said.
Earlier, the DOE said an investigation which began Nov 14 involved inspections of monitoring stations, field patrols and efforts to identify sources of pollution in the surrounding areas.
“Initial inspections found that the station was operating properly. However, further reviews are being conducted to verify the readings recorded.
“Patrols identified two small-scale open burning incidents, and both fires were extinguished on the same day,” the statement said.
The DOE reminded the public not to engage in open burning or allow their land and premises to be encroached upon by irresponsible parties, resulting in open burning, whether for specific purposes or accidentally.
Those convicted of an offence under Section 29(A) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 may face a fine of up to RM1 million or imprisonment for up to five years, or both, in addition to a compound of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine for each offence.
The public is also urged to help put out small fires and report open burning incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE’s toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727.
The latest hourly API readings can be accessed via the website at https://eqms.doe.gov.my/APIMS/main or the official MyJAS EQMS application, which can be downloaded from Google Play or the App Store. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Proposed Nutrition Bill, crypto mining woes and rural EV access
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The proposed Nutrition Bill, illegal cryptocurrency mining and the expansion of electric vehicle (EV) charging station infrastructure are among the issues to be discussed in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper published on Parliament’s official website, Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang) will ask the Health Minister during the oral question-and-answer session about the timeline for drafting the proposed Bill to regulate the nutritional intake of the public.
She also wants details on the Bill’s objectives, main scope, overall cost and mechanisms to ensure the participation of health experts, industry players, non-governmental organisations, the public and other stakeholders in its drafting and implementation.
In the same session, Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham (PH-Beruas) will ask the Home Minister why illegal cryptocurrency mining activities are rampant in Manjung, Perak, and why those involved are difficult to apprehend and bring to justice.
Meanwhile, Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Tun Hussein (BN-Sembrong) will ask the Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry about the ministry’s plans to expand EV charging station infrastructure to rural areas and small towns to encourage the adoption of green technology.
Also listed is a question from Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) to the Transport Minister on measures to improve safety management and emergency response at all short take-off and landing airports (STOLports) operating in Sarawak, following the helicopter crash in Long Lellang on Sept 8.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting will then proceed with the tabling of the Finance Bill 2026 and the Measures for the Collection, Administration and Enforcement of Tax Bill 2026 by the Finance Minister for first reading.
After that, the sitting will resume the committee-stage debate on the Supply (Budget 2027) Bill, followed by scheduled replies from the Works Ministry and the Transport Ministry.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, the committee-stage debate on Budget 2027 will continue until Nov 26, with 16 more ministries scheduled to conclude their respective winding-up sessions.
The Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament currently runs for 37 days until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: So, do you know what that Socso deduction in your payslip pays for?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — You see it every month on your payslip: a small deduction labelled Socso, amounting to just a few ringgit.
For some, they know that it is another statutory deduction made alongside their Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributions and income tax.
But not many know exactly what that money pays for.
Unlike EPF, which primarily helps Malaysians build retirement savings, the Social Security Organisation (Socso) or Perkeso (Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial) as it is sometimes referred to, provides protection against employment-related accidents, occupational diseases, permanent disability and certain other circumstances, depending on the scheme and eligibility requirements.
With Budget 2027 introducing new incentives to expand social protection among gig workers and the self-employed, you may want to pay attention to some of these changes.
Here is how Socso works, what is new and what to look out for.
What is Socso?
Socso is essentially designed to provide financial assistance, medical care and rehabilitation to eligible workers when circumstances affect their ability to earn a living.
For employees in the private sector, contributions are generally shared between employers and employees.
Under the standard First Category contribution scheme, which generally covers employees below 60 years old, employers contribute 1.75 per cent of an employee’s monthly wages while employees contribute 0.5 per cent, according to the prescribed contribution schedule.
This means the contribution is not borne entirely by workers, with employers paying the larger share.
The money goes towards financing social protection benefits rather than being accumulated in an individual savings account like EPF.
Socso administers several protection schemes, including the Employment Injury Scheme, Invalidity Scheme and the newer Non-Employment Injury Scheme, known as Lindung 24 Jam.
Socso administers several protection schemes, including the Employment Injury Scheme, Invalidity Scheme and the newer Non-Employment Injury Scheme, known as Lindung 24 Jam. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
How does Socso work?
One of Socso’s main functions is to protect employees against accidents that happen while carrying out their jobs.
However, its protection is not limited to accidents inside the workplace.
Under the Employment Injury Scheme, workers may also receive protection for commuting accidents, including those occurring while travelling between their homes and workplaces, provided they follow the route without an unauthorised interruption or deviation.
This means a worker who gets involved in an accident while travelling to work may qualify for Socso benefits, subject to the scheme’s conditions.
The protection also covers accidents during work-related journeys and certain emergencies at the workplace, as well as occupational diseases arising from employment.
Depending on the circumstances, eligible workers can receive several forms of assistance:
Medical benefits:
Medical treatment at Socso panel clinics or government hospitals for employment-related injuries or occupational diseases, subject to the applicable conditions.
Temporary disablement benefit:
Financial assistance when an employee is temporarily unable to work because of an employment injury.
The daily rate is generally 80 per cent of the employee’s average assumed daily wage, subject to prescribed minimum and maximum limits.
To qualify, the employee must be on medical leave certified by a doctor for at least four days, including the day of the accident. The benefit is not payable for days when the employee works and receives wages.
Permanent disablement benefit:
Financial assistance for workers who suffer permanent disabilities resulting from employment injuries. The daily rate is generally 90 per cent of the average assumed daily wage, subject to prescribed minimum and maximum limits and medical assessment.
Rehabilitation:
Physical and vocational rehabilitation, including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, prosthetics and skills training to help injured workers return to employment where possible.
Dependents’ benefit:
Financial assistance for eligible family members if an insured employee dies as a result of an employment injury.
Funeral benefit:
Financial assistance of up to RM3,000 for eligible cases, subject to the actual funeral expenses incurred.
Socso is not simply about reimbursing medical expenses as it also provides a measure of income protection when an accident prevents someone from returning to work.
Socso is not simply about reimbursing medical expenses as it also provides a measure of income protection when an accident prevents someone from returning to work. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Does Socso cover a person who becomes seriously ill outside of work?
Yes, it does but under a separate scheme.
The Invalidity Scheme provides 24-hour protection to eligible employees who suffer from a permanent medical condition, whether or not it is related to their employment.
To qualify, the condition must be certified by the Medical Board or Appellate Medical Board and leave the employee unable to earn at least one-third of the customary earnings of a healthy person with comparable abilities. Employees must also meet the scheme’s contribution requirements.
For example, an employee who develops a serious medical condition outside working hours that permanently affects their ability to earn a living may qualify for assistance.
Benefits include:
Invalidity pension:
A monthly pension for eligible employees who have been medically certified as suffering from invalidity and meet the contribution requirements.
Invalidity grant:
A lump-sum payment for eligible insured individuals who do not qualify for the monthly pension but meet the relevant contribution conditions.
Survivors’ pension:
Financial assistance for eligible dependents if an insured person dies, subject to the scheme’s conditions.
Rehabilitation:
Access to certain physical rehabilitation facilities and medical assistance, including dialysis.
Note that, while the Employment Injury Scheme covers accidents and occupational diseases arising from employment, the Invalidity Scheme provides protection against qualifying invalidity regardless of whether the condition is work-related.
In other words, Socso’s protection is not confined to accidents at the office or factory.
Can Socso protect you against accidents outside of working hours?
Yes. This is where the newer Non-Employment Injury Scheme, known as Lindung 24 Jam, comes in.
Introduced on June 1, 2026, the scheme extends protection to eligible employees who suffer accidental injuries outside working hours that are unrelated to their employment.
For example, an employee who is injured while carrying out personal activities during the weekend may qualify for protection under this scheme.
The benefits include medical treatment and other disablement benefits, subject to the scheme’s eligibility requirements.
However, Lindung 24 Jam does not cover every illness or accident.
Among its exclusions are:
Injuries caused by illnesses such as diabetes, fever and high blood pressure.
Accidents occurring outside Malaysia.
Injuries arising from self-employment, which fall under a separate social security scheme.
Domestic injuries covered under the Housewives’ Social Security Scheme.
Socso’s current guidance states that participation is voluntary for local employees, while it remains mandatory for foreign workers. Contributions are fully borne by employees who participate.
For local employees, this means the Lindung 24 Jam contribution is separate from the standard employment injury and invalidity contributions.
The contribution rate is being introduced in phases:
0.75 per cent for the first two years.
1 per cent for the following three years.
1.25 per cent from the sixth year onwards.
Employers are responsible for deducting and remitting the contribution for participating employees.
Unlike the standard Employment Injury and Invalidity schemes, employers do not share the cost of the Lindung 24 Jam contribution.
How much are you actually paying every month?
To put this into perspective, here is how much an employee would contribute at selected salary levels.
The standard First Category contribution is shared between employers and employees, while the additional Lindung 24 Jam contribution is borne entirely by employees who participate in the scheme.
https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30885188/
These figures follow Socso’s published Phase One contribution schedule. They exclude the Employment Insurance System (EIS), which is a separate contribution.
For local employees who do not participate in Lindung 24 Jam, the employee contribution is the standard Invalidity Scheme share shown in the table.
Employees can use Socso’s online contribution calculator to check their applicable contributions.
For employment-related accidents, employers are generally responsible for reporting the incident to Socso by submitting an Accident Report, known as Borang 34. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
How do you make a Socso claim?
If you are involved in a workplace accident or suffer an injury while commuting to work, you should inform your employer as soon as possible.
For employment-related accidents, employers are generally responsible for reporting the incident to Socso by submitting an Accident Report, known as Borang 34.
Supporting documents include:
A copy of the employee’s identification card.
Medical certificates or documents relating to the injury.
Attendance records or time cards.
A police report, where applicable.
For commuting accidents, employees may also need to provide a police report and a sketch map showing the route taken when the accident occurred.
Claims and supporting documents can be submitted through the relevant Socso application process, including the Lindung Faedah portal for applicable notices, or at a nearby Socso office.
For workers who are unsure whether their injuries qualify for coverage, they can contact Socso directly to clarify their eligibility and the documents required.
Claims and supporting documents can be submitted through the relevant Socso application process, including the Lindung Faedah portal for applicable notices, or at a nearby Socso office. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
What if an employer fails to pay Socso?
Seeing Socso deductions on your payslip does not necessarily mean your employer has actually remitted the contributions to Socso.
Employers are legally responsible for registering eligible employees and paying the required monthly contributions, including their own share.
Under the Employees’ Social Security Act 1969, employers who fail to register employees or pay contributions can face prosecution, with penalties of up to RM10,000 in fines, imprisonment of up to two years, or both upon conviction.
Employees with queries can raise the matter directly with Socso.
However, an employer’s failure to pay contributions does not automatically mean an injured employee loses all entitlement to benefits.
Under Section 48 of the Act, where an employer’s failure to pay a required contribution causes an employee or their dependents to qualify for benefits at a lower rate, Socso may pay the benefits at the rate they would have received had the contribution been made.
Socso can then recover from the employer either the difference between the benefits paid and the amount that should have been paid, or twice the amount of the unpaid contribution, whichever is greater.
The amount can be recovered as a debt owed to Socso. However, this provision does not apply to invalidity pensions.
Employees who suspect unpaid contributions should contact Socso to verify their records and benefits eligibility.
Can you claim tax relief for Socso contributions?
Yes. Budget 2027 proposes expanding tax relief to include mandatory contributions under Lindung Kendiri.
Taxpayers will also be eligible for additional tax relief of up to RM150 for qualifying voluntary contributions to Lindung 24 Jam and Lindung Kendiri.
The move is intended to encourage more self-employed individuals and employees to obtain additional social protection.
Who else benefits from the new Socso measures?
Budget 2027 also includes social protection measures for other groups.
For instance, contributions for approximately 40,000 religious personnel, including
imams, bilals, tok siak, noja, marbut
and
takmir
teachers, will be fully funded through Tabung Haji.
Separately, Socso will provide health screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers to help identify health risks that could affect their ability to drive safely.
These initiatives extend social protection to workers who may not necessarily fall under conventional employment arrangements.
Socso contributions may appear relatively small compared with other deductions on your payslip, but the protection they provide can become particularly important when an unexpected accident or illness affects your ability to earn an income. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
So, why should you care about that monthly deduction?
Socso contributions may appear relatively small compared with other deductions on your payslip, but the protection they provide can become particularly important when an unexpected accident or illness affects your ability to earn an income.
The important thing to remember is that Socso is not a personal savings account or a general insurance policy that automatically pays out for every accident or illness.
An employee’s eligibility to make Socso claims depends on the type of coverage, contribution record, medical assessment and eligibility conditions.
Hence, understanding what Socso covers is just as important as knowing how much is deducted from their salaries each month.

Title: From 328 to 56: Selangor flood hotspots down 82.9pc in 10 years, says MB
Article:
KLANG, Nov 15 — The number of flood hotspots in Selangor has dropped significantly by 82.9 per cent, from 328 areas in the 2016/2017 period to just 56 locations this year, following the implementation of various mitigation measures as well as continuous improvement of the drainage system by the state government.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said all the remaining high-risk locations identified were now being given special attention through an allocation for 47 mitigation projects aimed at reducing the impact of floods.
“We will focus on the 56 identified hotspots because the efforts we have undertaken in Selangor have proven effective in reducing and addressing flooding, including in Kampung Bukit Lanchong and Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, as well as several other areas.
“But we are now in the early stages of the monsoon transition, so we may have to see how it develops from time to time,” he told reporters after officiating at the launch of the 2026 National Digital Education Carnival for Parent, Community and Private Sector Engagement (PIBKS) at Klang Parade Mall here today.
Also present were Ministry of Education (MOE) Daily School Management Division director Mohd Hanafi Samad and Selangor Education director Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim.
Elaborating on the scope of the initiative, Amirudin said long-term plans were also being drawn up to address drainage problems in the Parit Mahang area in Kuala Selangor.
“This is an ongoing initiative and, certainly, three key areas have been identified, namely Kampung Melayu Subang, Kubu Gajah and Puncak Alam, which are being given attention as they have been affected by flooding, even during the early phase of the monsoon transition.
“Several districts which used to be badly affected, such as Dengkil, Kuala Langat and Hulu Langat, are now in a much more controlled situation following effective maintenance works and infrastructure upgrading carried out,” he added.
Earlier, the media reported that 1,399 evacuees from 370 families were still sheltering at six temporary relief centres in Kuala Selangor as of this afternoon, compared with 1,493 victims from 398 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, the Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang relief centre had the highest number of evacuees, at 420, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (391), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (287), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (119), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (114) and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (68). — Bernama

Title: Woman dies in two-car collision near Kota Tinggi after vehicle veers into oncoming traffic
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 15 — A 60-year-old woman was killed in an accident involving two cars at Kilometre 45 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Mersing near Kota Tinggi today.
Kota Tinggi district police chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received information from the public about the incident at 2 pm.
He said the accident involved a Toyota Vios driven by a 33-year-old man and a Proton Saga driven by a 28-year-old woman.
Yusof said the victim, who was the female driver’s mother, was travelling in the car with the driver’s two daughters, aged seven and five.
“Initial investigations found that the accident occurred when the Toyota Vios entered the opposite lane before colliding with the Proton Saga,” he said in a statement today.
He said the accident left the victim, who was seated in the rear right passenger seat, with severe internal injuries, and she was pronounced dead at the scene.
“The drivers of both vehicles and the children were taken to Kota Tinggi Hospital for further treatment,” he added.
Meanwhile, the victim’s body was sent to the Forensic Unit of the same hospital for further procedures. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute to be resolved soon, in line with state constitution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said the dispute involving the Negeri Sembilan royal and the state administration will be resolved soon in accordance with the state constitution.
He said the primary goal is to ensure the state administration runs smoothly for the people’s sake, according to a report by
The Star.
“The problems in Negeri Sembilan will be resolved as soon as possible,” he said after attending the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) Deepavali open house.
“We will do whatever necessary, provided that the problems faced by the people of Negeri are resolved and that the state administration runs smoothly and operates in accordance with the state constitution.”
The crisis began with a dispute between the four Undang and the 11th Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over who should be the state’s ruler.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim confirmed on September 17 that the state executive council backed an April 17 proclamation to unseat Tuanku Muhriz, which had been signed by one Undang and three other ruling chiefs whose positions were in dispute.
Ismail then sent a formal letter to the Conference of Rulers declaring Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the “new” Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
However, the state government officially withdrew that letter yesterday, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the state constitution and customary traditions.
The retraction took into account a statement issued by the Malay Rulers on October 14 as well as a Seremban High Court order dated June 5, which maintained the status quo regarding Tuanku Muhriz’s position.
Ismail said the decision to retract the letter was made to uphold the supremacy of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and preserve the order of constitutional monarchy.

Title: ‘We won big’: Sanusi wants PAS-led Perikatan-BN partnership to carry on to GE16
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 15 — PAS leader Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today said Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) should carry their partnership into the 16th general election after their win in the Melaka state election.
Sanusi, who is both PN and PAS election chief, said he hoped to see that happen after seeing how the majority of voters accepted the pairing,
Berita Harian
reported this evening.
“Alhamdulillah, we won big, more than before. I hope that is how it will be [for the cooperation to continue in the next general election],” he was quoted telling reporters after tabling the Kedah Budget 2027 at Wisma Darul Aman here.
He said the result also carried a message for the parties concerned, as voters had assessed current political developments for themselves.
Asked about his lighter presence on the Melaka campaign trail, Muhammad Sanusi said he had to concentrate on preparing the state budget, which required close scrutiny.
“I need to focus on Kedah Budget 2027 because it is longer, takes more time and is more detailed.
“We have to focus properly on the presentation, so there was no time. But there are plenty of others,” he was quoted as saying.
In yesterday’s Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats while the PAS-led PN three, giving the two sides a two-thirds majority between them, while Pakatan Harapan took four.
Bersatu, a PN component party, contested the election under its own logo, separately from PN, after falling out with PAS.

Title: Perikatan to decide stance on Sarawak polls as BN sits out, says Annuar Musa
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will determine its stance on contesting the upcoming Sarawak state election soon, according to its Information Chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa.
In a Facebook post today, Annuar stated that Barisan Nasional (BN) will not participate in the Sarawak polls, adding that not contesting might also be an option for PN.
This follows an announcement by BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi that the coalition will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election.
“BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” Zahid said.
Zahid, who is also Umno president and Deputy Prime Minister, explained that the decision aligns with the existing understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB).
The Election Commission has set December 12 as polling day for the Sarawak election, with nominations scheduled for November 28.

Title: GRS MPs to submit memorandum to PAC, seek expanded Pan Borneo probe
Article:
PAPAR, Nov 15 — Seven Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) Members of Parliament will submit a memorandum to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) next week seeking an expanded scope of investigation into the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, including an examination of the basis and implications of the decision to terminate the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019.
Papar MP Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. their spokesman, said the move was important to ensure that the PAC investigation not only focused on the project’s current status and performance, but also examined previous policy decisions allegedly affecting its implementation schedule, contractor appointments and rising construction costs.
Armizan, who is also GRS secretary-general, welcomed the PAC’s decision on October 19 to investigate the management, financial governance and physical implementation of the project following the tabling of the Auditor-General’s Report (AG’s Report) Series 2/2026.
However, he said the scope of the investigation should cover four key factors relating to the termination of the PDP model on September 22, 2019, to comprehensively identify the actual causes of the project’s delays.
“That is our recommendation to the PAC, that the scope of the investigation be expanded to cover the basis and implications of the termination of the PDP model,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the IP SPARK 2026 programme here today.
Elaborating, Armizan said the first factor was the lack of clarity regarding the implications of the PDP termination in the AG’s Report Series 2/2026, although official responses by the Works Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat on August 2, 2022 and October 19, 2026 had cited the termination of the model as one of the causes of project delays.
“So this is not political talk or political issues determined by people, but an official response in the Dewan Rakyat,” said Armizan, who is also Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister.
The second factor, he said, was the need to obtain clarification on the basis of the Federal Government’s decision to terminate the PDP model in 2019 following a recommendation by the Sabah state administration at the time, including whether a comprehensive study had been conducted before the decision was made.
On the third factor, he said uncertainty over the status of the PDP and contractor appointments following the change of government in May 2018 had allegedly caused construction work on the ground to stall for more than a year before existing contractors were reappointed under the conventional implementation method in 2019.
The disruption was also alleged to have contributed to higher project costs, particularly as contractors faced increases in construction material prices due to inflation, as well as the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said the fourth factor involved the process of reappointing existing contractors and appointing new ones, which was disrupted following the transition from the PDP model to the conventional method, resulting in some Phase 1A packages only undergoing the appointment process in 2021.
“So we hope that not only government agencies but also the contractors will be called to these proceedings to hear about the pressures and issues they faced,” he said.
He stressed that the GRS memorandum was not intended to find fault with any party, but to ensure that policy decisions concerning public infrastructure projects were not influenced by partisan political considerations to the detriment of their smooth implementation. — Bernama

Title: With MIC’s backing, BN vows to field PPP candidates in upcoming general election, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is committed to fielding candidates from the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) to represent the coalition in the upcoming 16th General Election (GE16).
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan remained steadfast alongside other coalition partners in efforts to revitalise the party as a new component member of BN.
“In my heart, alongside our partners from Umno, MCA and MIC, the PPP is also our partner.
“With the agreement of Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran (MIC president) and Datuk Seri M. Saravanan (MIC deputy president), I am determined that we will field PPP candidates in the upcoming general election,” he said in his speech at the Malaysia PPP Deepavali Open House here today.
On January 18, it was reported that PPP had been officially accepted as a component party of BN.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS), in a letter dated November 25, 2025, confirmed PPP’s status as a component party within the coalition. — Bernama

Title: Parit Yaani crash: Johor govt to bear medical costs, provide monthly aid to orphaned siblings, says exco
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Nov 15 — The Johor government, through the Johor State Islamic Religious Council (MAINJ), will cover the medical costs, including plastic surgery, for the two orphaned siblings who survived an accident along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar, near Parit Yaani, on November 1.
State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the assistance would also include a monthly allowance, as both children were orphaned following the tragedy.
He said the elder sibling, 11-year-old Hasya Fahira Zulkifli, had been readmitted to hospital and was scheduled to undergo plastic surgery on her leg, while her younger brother, Muhammad Adam Mohd Hardi, 8, was now able to walk but still required several follow-up treatments.
“MAINJ’s monthly financial assistance will continue until both siblings receive Survivors’ Pension benefits from the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO), as we understand their father had made contributions.
“The state government will continue to monitor the progress of both siblings… besides MAINJ, we have also been informed that the Social Welfare Department (JKM) is providing assistance,” he told reporters today.
He said this after accompanying Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi to visit Hasya Fahira at a ward at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI), where they also celebrated her 11th birthday today.
Elaborating, Mohd Fared said the state government was also prepared to cover other expenses should the need arise.
“Assistance of this nature is not limited to these two siblings but is extended to all Johoreans in need,” he added.
In the November 1 accident, which occurred at about 12.30pm, the siblings’ parents, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, and Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46, were killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they were traveling in was crushed by a tar-laden lorry, which had skidded following a tyre blowout.
In the incident, Mohd Hardi sustained serious injuries to his head and both hands, as well as burns to his body, while Tengku Syafirana suffered serious head and internal injuries, as well as burns to her body. — Bernama

Title: Vehicles over 5m barred from Sibu road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28 for festive decor
Article:
SIBU, Nov 15 — Vehicles exceeding five metres in height are prohibited from entering a designated road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28, 2027 to accommodate Christmas street lighting and festive decorations.
Sibu Municipal Council (SMC) in a statement said the restriction, which took effect on November 14, applies to the road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang, behind the WTK Holdings Berhad building.
The council said the temporary measure was necessary to ensure public safety as Christmas decorations and lighting installations would be suspended above the roadway.
SMC advised transport operators, lorry drivers, business operators and members of the public to plan their journeys accordingly and comply with all on-site instructions.
Meanwhile, the council said the Sibu Christmas Celebration 2026, themed ‘Lighting Up Sibu, Celebrating Christmas Together’, aimed to bring the community together, promote cultural harmony and share the joy of the festive season.
“Through the celebration, the council hopes to create a warm, joyful and welcoming festive environment where families, friends, residents and visitors of all ages can gather and enjoy the Christmas spirit,” it said.
SMC added that Christmas symbolised love, peace, hope and the spirit of giving, values that transcended racial, religious and cultural boundaries.
The council said the festive lighting and activities were also expected to enhance Sibu’s appeal, attract visitors and create business opportunities for local traders, food operators and the tourism industry.
SMC thanked the public for their understanding and cooperation in observing the temporary restriction and invited everyone to take part in the Christmas celebration. — The Borneo Post

Title: Senator warns early Parliament dissolution could derail Budget 2027 and force temporary spending, citing 2022 precedent
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 15 — Calls for an early dissolution of the Dewan Rakyat are ill-timed as Budget 2027 has yet to complete the parliamentary approval process, said Senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim.
He said dissolving Parliament before the Budget was passed could disrupt the government’s financial planning and delay funding for development projects, infrastructure programmes and other public commitments.
Ahmad said that while the Prime Minister could seek the dissolution of Parliament under the Federal Constitution, subject to the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the timing of such a move should be carefully considered.
“My concern is not about whether Parliament can be dissolved, but whether this is the appropriate time to do so,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad, who chairs the Senate Select Committee on National Defence and Security, pointed out that Budget 2027, involving hundreds of billions of ringgit in government expenditure, was still undergoing parliamentary scrutiny.
The Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to complete its committee-stage deliberations on November 26, while the Dewan Negara will begin its deliberations on November 30.
Ahmad said the legislative process should be allowed to run its course, warning that dissolving Parliament before the Supply Bill completes the approval process could result in it lapsing.
“This would require a new government and Parliament to reintroduce and approve the Budget, potentially delaying financial authorisations needed to sustain government operations and implement planned programmes.
“Although temporary expenditure arrangements could be made under constitutional provisions, these would still require further legislative action,” he said.
He cited the October 2022 dissolution of Parliament, which took place just three days after Budget 2023 was tabled.
Following the formation of a new government, Parliament had to approve about RM107.7 billion in temporary operating expenditure in December 2022 to ensure that government operations could continue pending approval of the full Budget.
“Why unnecessarily risk repeating such complications?”
Ahmad said Malaysia was already facing an increasingly uncertain global environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, economic instability, employment concerns, food security issues and the rising cost of living.
“The last thing we need is additional uncertainty surrounding our national financial planning,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kedah aims to cut operating deficit to 10.59pc with RM1.34b Budget 2027, says MB
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 15 — The Kedah state government today tabled its RM1.34 billion Budget 2027, projecting an operating deficit of RM90 million or 10.59 per cent, for the year.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the state government had estimated revenue of RM850 million under the budget, themed ‘The Greater Kedah: Mensejahterakan Rakyat’, while operating expenditure was projected at RM940 million.
He said the revenue target represented an increase of RM12 million from the RM838 million targeted in 2026, with land revenue contributing the largest share at RM551 million, followed by miscellaneous revenue (RM253 million), forestry revenue (RM30 million) and district revenue (RM16 million).
“Of the total operating expenditure allocation, RM81.66 million is set aside for charged expenditure, while RM858.34 million is allocated for supply and services expenditure.
“The 2027 Budget also includes allocations for the State Development Fund, Forest Development Fund and Water Supply Development Fund, with total development expenditure amounting to RM401.28 million,” he said when tabling the Kedah Budget 2027 at the Kedah State Legislative Assembly sitting at Wisma Darul Aman here today.
He said RM245 million of the development allocation was set aside for the State Development Fund, involving 10 implementing departments, while RM12.53 million was allocated for forestry development.
The Water Supply Development Fund received RM143.75 million, comprising RM138.75 million from federal government loans for the implementation of three loan-funded projects and RM5 million from the state government’s allocation.
“The state government also aims to gradually reduce its operating deficit to 10.59 per cent in 2027, from 12.65 per cent in 2025 and 11.81 per cent in 2026.
“This reflects the state government’s commitment to strengthening its fiscal position through expenditure controls, improved management efficiency and optimisation of state revenue sources to ensure long-term financial sustainability,” he said.
The 2027 Budget is the second year of the implementation of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), continuing the state’s development agenda based on the Kedah Development Plan 2035 and The Greater Kedah 2050, with emphasis on ensuring that economic progress also improves the people’s well-being. — Bernama

Title: BN to skip Sarawak state polls under Umno-PBB understanding, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
The decision is in line with an understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said.
“BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” he told reporters at the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) Deepavali open house here today.
Also present were PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan and MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Dec 12 as polling day, with nomination scheduled for Nov 28
On the possibility of Parliament being dissolved, Ahmad Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said the decision rested with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying that he (Anwar) has the right and mandate to do so.
On the political crisis in Negeri Sembilan, Ahmad Zahid said efforts would be made to resolve the situation as soon as possible.
He said the necessary steps would be taken to address the problems faced.
“What matters is that the people’s problems in Negeri Sembilan are resolved and that the state administration runs smoothly and in accordance with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Do not be alarmed’: MetMalaysia to conduct tsunami warning siren test in Kudat tomorrow
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 15 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) will conduct a siren test for the Malaysian Tsunami Early Warning System (SAATNM) at the Kudat District Police Headquarters (IPD) tomorrow.
In a post on Facebook, MetMalaysia said the test is scheduled to take place between 9 am and noon.
“Residents in the surrounding areas are advised not to be alarmed by the sound of the sirens, as this is merely a test.
“MetMalaysia will provide updates should there be any changes,” the statement read. — Bernama

Title: Ageing 40-year-old water tank bursts in Kuala Kangsar, affecting 520 consumers; no damage or injuries reported
Article:
IPOH, Nov 15 — The bursting of a 455-cubic-metre water tank at Taman Kuala Kangsar in Kuala Kangsar yesterday was caused by the condition of its structure, which was more than 40 years old.
Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Kuala Kangsar operations centre of the Perak Water Board (LAP) received information about the incident at about 5pm, which affected water supply to approximately 520 consumers in the surrounding areas.
He said LAP had carried out washing and cleaning works on roads around the burst Taman Kuala Kangsar tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline to the affected areas, namely Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti, had also been implemented.
“The removal of all affected tank panels has been carried out, and plans are being made to replace the tank with a new one.
“In addition, LAP is conducting a comprehensive technical assessment of the old tank structure before installation of the new tank begins,” he said in a statement today.
Mohammad Nizar said preliminary investigations at the scene found that the burst tank had caused water to overflow onto surrounding roads, but no reports of casualties or property damage had been received so far.
“An inspection of the house located nearest to the tank also found that it was safe and had sustained no damage,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Nizar said water supply in the affected areas remained stable and uninterrupted, and the Kuala Kangsar LAP operations centre would continue to monitor the situation to ensure there were no disruptions to water supply and to prevent a recurrence.
Several videos of the tank bursting incident have gone viral on social media since yesterday, causing panic among residents. — Bernama

Title: Selangor flood evacuees fall to 1,399; Perak down to 191
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak declined as of 4pm today.
In SELANGOR, 1,399 people from 370 families were still taking shelter at six relief centres in Kuala Selangor, down from 1,493 people from 398 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang recorded the highest number of evacuees at 420, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (391), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (287), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (119), KAFA Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (114) and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (68).
In PERAK, the number of evacuees also fell to 191 people from 58 families, compared with 293 people from 85 families this morning.
All 191 evacuees were housed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council’s Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the SK Khir Johari relief centre in Muallim, which had accommodated 94 people from 25 families, was closed after floodwaters in Kampung Berop receded completely. — Bernama

Title: One hour of rain, roads under water: Flash floods hit Shah Alam’s i-City
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 15 — More than an hour of continuous heavy rain caused flash floods along roads in the i-City and Section 7 areas here, disrupting traffic movement this afternoon.
Posts shared by users on the Threads application showed floodwaters inundating the areas following heavy rain which began at about 1pm.
A user, frhn.jefx, posted a video showing a flooded road near i-City, with several vehicles, particularly motorcycles, forced to stop along the stretch.
Another user, jacketpotato.sa, also shared information on conditions along the same route, showing several cars making their way through the floodwaters.
Another user, charlie.kilo.maggi, shared footage of flash flooding at 2.46pm along the exit from the i-City area.
“Had to take a detour via the area behind the factories (around the Pharmaniaga factory) to get out. Hope everyone stays safe,” the post said.
Meanwhile, a user, sashidd, posted a video on the same application showing flooding at a car park in Section 7 and advised the public to abandon plans to visit the area to avoid getting stranded.
Earlier, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in nine states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 5pm today.
In Selangor, the areas expected to be affected are Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Kuala Selangor and Hulu Langat. — Bernama

Title: Seats, candidates, strategy — Sarawak DAP will decide, says Loke
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 15 — DAP has given full autonomy to the Sarawak DAP leadership to decide how many seats to contest, who to field and its strategy for the upcoming Sarawak state election, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said.
He said that after yesterday’s Melaka state election, the party’s focus has shifted to preparing for the polls in the Land of the Hornbills.
“All decisions concerning the Sarawak state election will be made by Sarawak DAP. The party has indeed granted Sarawak DAP autonomy to make decisions on the number of seats, candidates and strategies,” he told a press conference at the 2026 Johor DAP Convention here today.
He said the central leadership would continue to provide strong support to ensure the smooth running of the party’s machinery in Sarawak.
Asked about the party’s seat projections and the challenges it would face in the state election, Loke said details would be announced by the Sarawak DAP leadership at an appropriate time.
“Of course, some may ask whether it will be a tough election. Definitely, all elections are tough; no election is easy,” he said.
The Election Commission has set Dec 12 as polling day, Nov 28 for nomination and Dec 8 for early voting. — Bernama

Title: From setbacks to comeback? Dzulkefly wants Amanah ready for GE16
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 15 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) must use its defeats in several state elections as a springboard to strengthen the party and prepare its machinery for the 16th General Election (GE16), its vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
He said the entire party leadership and machinery, particularly the youth and young women, must self-reflect, strengthen the organisation and devise more effective strategies for reaching out to the people.
He said the defeats in past elections should serve as a lesson and a catalyst for building new strength, rather than weakening morale or confidence in the party’s struggle.
“We may have lost some battles, but we must make sure we are better prepared to reach the people,... we have lost the battle, but we want to win the war. In the GE16 war to come, we will do our best,” he told reporters after officiating the Wanita Muda Amanah national convention (Warda) here today.
Dzulkefly said Amanah’s struggle should not be centred solely on electoral victory; rather, political victory must serve as a means to build a united, strong and dignified nation-state grounded in the values of human dignity (karamah insaniah).
In his speech, he said the party’s goal is to uphold the dignity of every individual regardless of race, religion, ancestry or social standing, while celebrating diversity in society.
“Victory is not everything; it is the means to an end — a means to a higher and nobler goal. We want to drive a united, strong and dignified nation-state that celebrates diversity,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly described the country’s economic performance under the Unity Government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as commendable compared with previous decades, citing positive economic growth, rising foreign investment, low inflation and unemployment, and a strengthening ringgit.
He said these achievements should be leveraged by Amanah to bolster public confidence in the Unity Government, and to ensure that the government’s policies and successes are translated into a political approach close to the pulse of the people.
On GE16, Dzulkefly said there was no need for the general election to be held in the near future, and that it should instead be held in accordance with the parliamentary term.
He said the government need not rush to dissolve Parliament, as the current focus is on sustaining economic growth momentum and strengthening the country’s financial position and industrial sector. — Bernama
